extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / citizens interested in postwar moral and political issues
extracted.subtask_description: A mid-20th-century newspaper page combining an editorial/Christmas message (moral guidance on church, peace, and prisoners) with news dispatches about postwar events. Content is aimed at informing and morally addressing the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supranational character of the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: She is supranational ... she extends the same love to all nations and peoples; she lives and grows in all countries of the world, and they all contribute to her life and growth. She does not cut off or destroy any of [diverse customs, laws, institutions], but rather preserves and observes them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that ecclesiastical life once flowed from old Europe but now is shared between all members of the mystical body; cites St. Augustine: the church 'recruits her citizens from all nations' and 'in every language assembles her community of pilgrims on earth.' The church should draw on local customs and direct differences to the common end of peace, as long as they do not impede worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration and reciprocal confidence for lasting peace
rubrics_metrics.description: The present hour calls imperiously for collaboration, reciprocal confidence in all peoples. The motives of hate, vengeance, rivalry, antagonism, unfair and dishonest competition must be kept out of political and economic debates and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political and economic deliberations should exclude hate and vengeance; public actors must not do to others what they denounce. Quotation from Proverbs supports moral purity. This principle underpins the broader 'peace structure' discussion and is presented as a primary moral prerequisite for a true and lasting peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparations and claims must be based on moral principles and respect inviolable natural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: One who seeks reparations should base his claim on moral principles, respect for those inviolable natural rights which remain valid even for those who have surrendered unconditionally to the victor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admonishes that in seeking justice one must avoid repeating the misdeeds one decries; claims should not justify doing to others what was wrong when done to oneself. Emphasizes restraint and moral grounding in settlement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: True security rests on internal societal strength (family, labor, fraternal charity)
rubrics_metrics.description: One who asks for security in the future should not forget that its only true guarantee lies in one’s own internal force—that is, in safeguarding the family, labor, in fraternal charity, the outlawing of all hate, all persecution, all unjust vexation of honest citizens, in loyal concord between State and State, between people and people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-makers should prioritize strengthening domestic social structures—family stability, labor protections, social charity—over reliance on external coercive guarantees. This is presented as a practical moral foundation for lasting peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject artificial manipulation of public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Men must everywhere forego the artificial creation, through the power of wealth, of arbitrary one-sided judgments and false assertions, of a so-called public opinion which sways the ideas and will of the electorate like reeds shaken by the wind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges caution against wealthy or powerful interests manufacturing consensus; calls to heed the 'true and overwhelming majority' made up of honest, peace-loving working families when making political decisions about borders and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totalitarianism is incompatible with true democracy and peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Totalitarianism lowers man to the state of a mere pawn in the game of politics ... it drives millions of men ... into the most squalid misery ... Within the confines of each particular nation as much as in the whole family of peoples, state totalitarianism is incompatible with a true and healthy democracy. Like a dangerous germ it infects the community of nations and renders it incapable of guaranteeing the security of individual peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates concrete harms of totalitarian policies: arbitrary frontier changes, economic dispossession, forced migrations, restriction of migration/colonization rights, and rendering peoples' welfare subordinate to vested interests. Presents outlawing totalitarian aggression and oppression as necessary to prevent future wars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlaw aggressive use of force and ban all oppression and arbitrary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The future peace structure aims at outlawing from the world every aggressive use of force, every war of aggression. But if this is to be something more than a beautiful gesture, all oppression and all arbitrary action from within and without must be banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames legal/political prohibitions (outlawing wars of aggression) as insufficient alone; stresses that internal oppression must also be addressed for genuine, enforceable peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return to God and Christian moral order in politics as remedy for moral collapse
rubrics_metrics.description: There remains but one solution: a return to God and to the order established by Him ... If the root of the evil lies in neglect, overthrow, denial and contempt of Christian thought ... there is but one remedy: to go back to the order fixed by God also in relations between states and peoples; to go back to a real Christianity within the state and among states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that policies guided by eternal truths and laws of God are the most realistic and durable; presents 'real Christianity' in public life as practical political realism rather than impractical idealism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane treatment, timely liberation, and fair rehabilitation of prisoners and deported persons
rubrics_metrics.description: These unfortunate victims must be treated in a humane manner ... the much-desired pacification and concord among peoples could not be better initiated than by their liberation and as far as possible by their fair, proper and equitable rehabilitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condemns prolonging captivity without reasonable cause, subjecting prisoners to hard and unjustified labor, and refusing treatment due under international conventions and Christian and civil conscience; urges speedy return of service members to families and inclusion of political prisoners, missionaries and civilians in relief and repatriation efforts.
